mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days, reflecting stronger labor market conditions and increased consumer spending.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses below 3.5%, or returns revert to baseline within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDPC1 (total demand) and HOUST (industrial production) signals robust demand-side expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 and HOUST are rising concurrently, or returns decline despite the proxies' upward trends.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (rising FEDFUNDS), sustained increases in the federal funds rate compress discount rates, enhancing equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods identified as tightening cycles, or returns revert to baseline within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid monthly increase in the CPIAUCSL index exceeding 1% triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, reflecting inflationary pressures that erode equity valuations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when CPIAUCSL crosses above the 1% MoM threshold, or returns revert to baseline within 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) exceeding 5% triggers positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, signaling strong labor market growth and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS rises by >5% MoM, or returns decline despite the trigger occurring.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and decline in UNRATE (unemployment) indicates an expansionary monetary policy and labor market recovery, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS ↑ and UNRATE ↓ occur concurrently, or returns revert to baseline within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion phase (high GDPC1 growth), a sustained rise in GDPC1 triggers positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as excess demand drives equity valuations higher.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 rises above its 12-month average, or returns revert to baseline within 120 days.
